summary.one_liner: Magick is a visual, node-based AI development environment for building no-code data pipelines and multimodal agents.
summary.what_it_does: Magick lets users build AI workflows as graphs: nodes perform transformations on data, and wires (connections) pass data and triggers between them. Each graph and its data, variables, and presets is saved as a "spell," which is exported as JSON. The README describes nodes such as Input, Prompt Template, Code, Generator, and Wait For All, with some nodes defining custom inputs and outputs. It mentions social connectors to Discord, Twitter, and Twilio, search via Google, Wikipedia, and the Semantic Web, and tools for voice and image generation and vector search. Graphs can be embedded as subgraphs and shared. The README says the project is based on the archived Thoth project by Latitude Games.
use_cases: connect AI workflows to Discord or Twitter
prototype multimodal agents with voice and image generation
how_to_run: Follow the macOS, Linux, or Windows installation guide linked in the README
Set up the environment and database as described in the installation guide
Consult the Development Guide and Architecture Overview for development setup
notable: Visual node-based composer for AI pipelines with no coding required
Spells: graphs with data, variables and presets exported as shareable JSON
Subgraphs that can be embedded and shared with the community
Realtime agents with unified memory that act on their own and interact across modalities
Based on the archived Thoth project by Latitude Games
caveats: Several connectors (Zoom, Google Meet, Reddit, Slack) are described as 'coming soon' as plugins, not yet available
Installation requires following OS-specific guides that include environment and database configuration
README does not state the license
